"'''Watch Me'''" (also known as "'''Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)'''") is the debut single by American rapper [[Silentó]]. In March 2015, he was signed to [[Capitol Records]], which released the track as a single with an accompanying music video. The song peaked at number three on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], where it spent six non-consecutive weeks. With a viral clip on [[YouTube]], the song was popular for its dance despite negative reviews, a combination of two popular moves cited in the title: the "Whip" and the "[[Nae Nae]]"<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/lists/2015s-10-most-viewed-music-videos-on-youtube-20151209 | title=2015's 10 Most Viewed Music Videos on YouTube | date=December 9, 2015 | first=Brittany | last=Stanos | magazine=Rolling Stone | access-date=July 5, 2016}}</ref> as well as other [[hip hop dance]]s from various songs, such as "[[Crank That (Soulja Boy)]]" and "[[Stanky Legg]]".

"Watch Me" (also known as "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)") is the debut single by American rapper Silentó. In March 2015, he was signed to Capitol Records, which released the track as a single with an accompanying music video. The song peaked at number three on the Billboard Hot 100, where it spent six non-consecutive weeks. With a viral clip on YouTube, the song was popular for its dance despite negative reviews, a combination of two popular moves cited in the title: the "Whip" and the "Nae Nae" as well as other hip hop dances from various songs, such as "Crank That (Soulja Boy)" and "Stanky Legg".

[[File:SFOT Whip-NaeNae.webm|thumb|Whip and Nae Nae performed at [[Six Flags Over Texas]]]]
The music video was uploaded online on Silentó's [[Vevo]] channel on [[YouTube]] on June 25, 2015, and shot in Atlanta, Georgia. It was directed by [[Marc Klasfeld]]. Set in a high school gymnasium, Silentó performs the dance moves mentioned in the song with dance crews, high school, and university cheerleaders, fans, even a trio of older conservative white women who later join in on the dance, and also incorporates videos sent in by viewers. [[Lil Scrappy]] and [[Rich White Ladies]] make guest appearances in the video.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dB5PtqPcXPg "Watch Me: Behind the Scenes"] from [[YouTube]] (Posted July 21, 2015)</ref>  As of June 2025, it has surpassed 1.9 billion views on YouTube.<ref>{{Citation|last=SilentoVEVO|title=Silentó – Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae) (Official)|date=June 25, 2015|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vjW8wmF5VWc|access-date=August 17, 2016}}</ref>

The digital media company DanceOn was crucial to the success of "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)." After striking a deal with Silentó, DanceOn reached out to its network of dance content creators to make instructional videos to the song for their #WatchMeDanceOn campaign. 50 of their creators made videos that they then posted on YouTube. Instantly they gained popularity bringing in more than 250 million views in under three months.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/madonna-cofounded-a-company-that-creates-viral-dance-videos-and-whipnae-nae-was-its-first-monster-hit-2016-1|title=Madonna cofounded a startup that manufactures viral dance trends — and 'Whip/Nae Nae' was its first monster hit|work=Business Insider|access-date=December 9, 2017|language=en}}</ref>  The campaign was launched on April 13, 2015, and by May 22, 2015, the track's sales tripled from 17,000 units a week to 42,000 a week.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/atlanta-rapper-silentos-road-to-a-label-deal-chart-success/|title=Atlanta Rapper Silento's Road to a Label Deal, Chart Success: Professional YouTubers|magazine=Billboard|access-date=December 9, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=Silento's 'Watch Me' Whip/Nae Nae Lesson - So You Know You Can't Dance Ep. 9 | date=July 9, 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pT3gGhTtJAQ |access-date=2023-09-14 |language=en}}</ref>

The digital media company DanceOn was crucial to the success of "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)." After striking a deal with Silentó, DanceOn reached out to its network of dance content creators to make instructional videos to the song for their #WatchMeDanceOn campaign. 50 of their creators made videos that they then posted on YouTube. Instantly they gained popularity bringing in more than 250 million views in under three months.  The campaign was launched on April 13, 2015, and by May 22, 2015, the track's sales tripled from 17,000 units a week to 42,000 a week.

sections.heading: Commercial
sections.wikitext: "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)" peaked at number three on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], where it has spent six non-consecutive weeks being kept from number one on the chart by songs such as "[[Cheerleader (Omi song)|Cheerleader]]" by [[Omi (singer)|Omi]] and "[[Can't Feel My Face]]" by [[The Weeknd]]. It spent eighteen weeks in the top ten of that chart before dropping out on October 14, 2015.<ref name="US">{{cite web|title=Silento Chart History|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/6495286/silento/chart|website=Billboard.com|access-date=June 14, 2015}}</ref> Streaming and downloads propped up its run on the chart the most, while radio play was only moderate. It reached number three on the [[Digital Song Sales|download component chart]] and topped the [[Streaming Songs|streaming chart]] for ten weeks, while barely missing the top 20 for the [[Radio Songs (chart)|radio chart]], peaking at 22.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/silento/chart-history/HDS/|title=Silento Chart History (Digital Song Sales)|work=Billboard|access-date=January 25, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/silento/chart-history/stm/|title=Silento Chart History (Streaming Songs)|work=Billboard|access-date=January 25, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/silento/chart-history/HSB/|title=Silento Chart History (Radio Songs)|work=Billboard|access-date=January 25, 2026}}</ref> Internationally, the song has peaked within the top ten of the charts in Australia, as well as the top twenty of the charts in Denmark, New Zealand and the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acharts.co/song/91107|title=Watch Me (Whip / Nae Nae)|work=acharts.co|access-date=October 30, 2015}}</ref>  The song reached over 2 million in sales by November 2015,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hiphopdx.com/news/id.36270/title.hip-hop-single-sales-drake-justin-timberlake-the-weeknd |title=Hip Hop Single Sales: Drake, Justin Timberlake & The Weeknd |last=Mansell |first=Henry |website=[[HipHopDX]] |publisher=Cheri Media Group |date=November 14, 2015 |access-date=November 14, 2015}}</ref> and has sold 2,440,000 copies as of June 2016.<ref name="us sales">{{cite news|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160705145725/http://www.defjampromo.com/files/2009/10/BB-Digital-Songs-Chart-Wk.-Ending-6-16-16.pdf|title=Nielsen SoundScan charts – Digital Songs – Week Ending: 06/06/2016|publisher=[[Nielsen SoundScan]]|url=http://www.defjampromo.com:80/files/2009/10/BB-Digital-Songs-Chart-Wk.-Ending-6-16-16.pdf|archive-date=July 5, 2016|access-date=August 1, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>
sections.text: "Watch Me (Whip/Nae Nae)" peaked at number three on the Billboard Hot 100, where it has spent six non-consecutive weeks being kept from number one on the chart by songs such as "Cheerleader" by Omi and "Can't Feel My Face" by The Weeknd. It spent eighteen weeks in the top ten of that chart before dropping out on October 14, 2015. Streaming and downloads propped up its run on the chart the most, while radio play was only moderate. It reached number three on the download component chart and topped the streaming chart for ten weeks, while barely missing the top 20 for the radio chart, peaking at 22. Internationally, the song has peaked within the top ten of the charts in Australia, as well as the top twenty of the charts in Denmark, New Zealand and the United Kingdom.  The song reached over 2 million in sales by November 2015, and has sold 2,440,000 copies as of June 2016.

sections.heading: Critical
sections.wikitext:
[[Elliott Wilson (journalist)|Elliot Wilson]] listed it #2 on his list of 15 worst singles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://rapradar.com/features/15-worst-singles-1-wiz-khalifa-see-you-again/|title='15 Worst Singles #1: Wiz Khalifa "See You Again"|website=Rap Radar|date=January 8, 2016 }}</ref> [[Complex (magazine)|Complex]] called it "one of the most annoying things to ever exist", and listed it among their "Songs We Hated in 2015".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2015/12/worst-songs-of-2015/|title=Songs We Hated in 2015|website=Complex}}</ref>

It received a nomination for Song of the Summer at the [[2015 MTV Video Music Awards]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Song of Summer|url=http://www.mtv.com/ontv/vma/2015/song-of-summer/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150820032658/http://www.mtv.com/ontv/vma/2015/song-of-summer/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 20, 2015|publisher=MTV|access-date=August 19, 2015}}</ref> and another nomination for R&B/Hip-Hop Song at the [[Teen Choice Awards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chiff.com/pop-culture/teen-choice-awards.htm|title=2015 Teen Choice Awards, Nominees, Winners, TV Schedule|work=chiff.com|access-date=October 30, 2015}}</ref>
